messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test "testBinaryEncoder()" verifies that the Base64 instance encoder encodes bytes exactly as UTF-8 bytes of a corresponding string (line 411). This test fails because the instance method encode() of Base64 appends an additional CRLF (line separator) and chunks outputs into 76 character lines, which was not the behavior in Commons-Codec 1.3 but is present in 1.4.

From the Base64 constructor chain, the default constructor Base64() calls Base64(false), which calls Base64(int lineLength, byte[] lineSeparator, boolean urlSafe) with defaults. The default constructor sets line length and lineSeparator to chunk the output and append a line separator (usually CRLF) every 76 characters.

The encode(byte[] pArray) method (lines 928-950) calculates the encoded length including space for chunk separators by calling getEncodeLength() (lines 963-980) which adds chunkSeparator length if chunking is enabled (line 972-978).

In the encode(byte[], int, int) method (lines 452-513), when encoding completes (EOF notified by inAvail < 0, line 458), the method appends a lineSeparator if lineLength > 0 and pos > 0 (line 484-487). Also during encoding, if current line length reaches lineLength (76), it appends the lineSeparator (line 505-509).

Therefore, the instance encode() encodes with chunking and line separators by default, appending a trailing CRLF, which differs from the static encodeBase64() method behavior and previous version 1.3 without chunking.

The test fails because it compares strict equality of encoded byte arrays expecting no trailing CRLF. The added CRLF and chunking cause Arrays.equals() to return false.

In summary:
- The Base64 instance encode() method chunks output and appends line separators by default.
- This causes additional trailing CRLF(s) not expected in the test.
- The test strictly compares encoded bytes to unchunked raw UTF-8 bytes.
- This behavior changed from version 1.3 to 1.4 causing test failure.

The root cause is the default enabled chunking (lineLength > 0) and appending line separators in the instance Base64 encoder by default.

Since the test uses new Base64() (lines 408), the chunking and trailing CRLF insertion behavior triggers and causes test failure.

Recent bug reports do not add relevant information beyond this root cause analysis.

This matches the issue described in the current bug report - new Base64().encode() appends CRLF and chunks output into 76-character lines.

Thus the bug is that the default Base64 instance encoder appends chunk separators (CRLF) and line breaks during encoding, differing from previous behavior and causing compatibility issues in tests relying on unchunked output.

Recommended fixes would involve either disabling chunking by default or adjusting encode() behavior or tests to accommodate this chunking behavior.

Next I will suggest which methods to fix.
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64.encode(byte[])
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64.Base64()
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64.encode(byte[], int, int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
